evidence: AppointmentsController.book maps BookingForm fields, including `new Date(form.startsAt)`, and hands the work to `this.scheduling.book`, then calls `present(...)`.
AppointmentsController.cancel hands the work to `this.scheduling.cancel(id, new Date())` and presents the result.
AppointmentsController.addNote hands the work to `this.notes.write` and `this.notes.notesFor`, then returns a `{ count }` response object.
BookingForm and NoteForm are input data shapes for the presentation layer and contain no logic.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The controller does only presentation work. It defines input form shapes, turns transport values into domain call arguments (it parses the string date and supplies the current time for cancel), hands each request to business services, and formats the output through the presenter or a small response object. It has no business rules such as overlap checks, booking validation or note policies. It has no persistence logic and no framework or transport plumbing beyond mapping requests to calls. Counting notes with `.length` in addNote only shapes the response. It is not a domain rule.
